headline: Forum Dedicated to Ranking Elevator Music Releases Controversial 'GOAT List'
subheadline: Community explodes after 'Girl From Ipanema (Smooth Jazz Arrangement #7)' ranked above 'Muzak Opus 847'
summary: The internet's most dedicated elevator music enthusiasts are at war over their definitive rankings.
content:
The MyFace group "Elevator Music Appreciation Society" has released its annual ranking of greatest elevator music tracks, and the community is in chaos after the results placed a relatively obscure bossa nova cover above the legendary "Muzak Opus 847."

"This is a travesty," wrote longtime member @LiftListener. "Opus 847 defined the genre. It's been playing in the Hartwell Building lobby since 1987. It's the reason I got into elevator music. And you're telling me a Girl From Ipanema variant beats it?"

The community, founded in 2018, has 23,000 members who collect, catalog, and critique background music designed to be ignored. They maintain a database of over 12,000 tracks including building-specific recordings captured via smartphone.

"Most people don't even hear elevator music," explained founder @MuzakMonarch. "We hear nothing else. Every saxophone line. Every pan flute. Every inexplicable vibraphone choice. We're listening to what you tune out."

The ranking methodology considers multiple factors: melodic inoffensiveness, background blendability, tempo consistency, and "how many times you can hear it before wanting to scream." Top tracks achieve what members call "audio wallpaper perfection."

The society has developed a genre taxonomy including "Smooth Waiting" (jazz-influenced), "Corporate Calm" (synthesizer-heavy), "Retail Fog" (shopping center variants), and "Hold Music Horrors" (technically different but often discussed).

"People think we're joking," said member @AmbientArchivist. "We're not. Elevator music is the most listened-to genre on earth. Billions of hours annually. Someone should take it seriously. That someone is us."

The controversy has sparked breakaway factions. A splinter group called "True Muzak Heads" has formed, dedicated exclusively to pre-2000 recordings. They dismiss modern elevator music as "too produced."

At stake is more than pride. The top-ranked track receives a custom plaque that members have successfully placed in 847 elevator lobbies worldwide, often without building management noticing.

"That's the highest honor," said @MuzakMonarch. "Anonymous recognition. Just like the music itself."
author: Jennifer Park, Culture Reporter
